accuracy.evidence: Content matches Common Core SL.5.1c (pose and respond to specific questions, make comments that contribute to the discussion and elaborate on the remarks of others) and the topic evidence lines: follow-up questions that build on a comment, adding evidence or an example to a classmate's idea, and redirecting with a question that connects to the main topic. Every keyed answer was checked so that only one option builds, follows up, gives evidence or steers back; distractors are clearly repeat, off-topic, vague, no-reason, drift, rude or about the person.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the habits described by Mercer and Dawes (exploratory talk) and Michaels, O'Connor and Resnick (Accountable Talk): repeating a point in new words and calling it agreement (step 0 card, tag 'repeat', p1, m2), off-topic personal remarks (tags 'offtopic'), vague questions (step 4 sort, tag 'vague', p3, m6), opinions with no reason (step 2 prediction, tag 'noreason', m4), following a drift (step 3, tag 'drift', m5), shutting people down (tag 'rude') and commenting on the person not the idea (tag 'person', m9).

lab_distinct.evidence: The lab models a live discussion around one question: a reply slot with a 'how far the talk moves' meter that stays still for a repeat and drops for an off-topic remark, follow-up questions keyed to Leo's exact remark, a drag-to-attach evidence board linking facts to remarks, a drifting chain of bubbles with a distance-from-the-question meter that resets only for a linking question, and a vague/specific sorter. No other flagship lab has discussion moves; gate_lab_distinct passes against flaglisten, flagwonder and flagquote.

lab_teaches.evidence: Learners act before the rule is named: placing 'I agree, more time to play' leaves the meter still with feedback that it repeats Ava, while 'Yes, and running around could help us focus' fills it. In step 3 the follow-the-drift reply pushes the meter to 'even further from the question'. Each done line states the rule just shown ('keep the idea, add something new', 'a linking question steers drifting talk back').

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options the lab tests: which kind of reply moves a discussion forward (saying the same idea again versus adding something new), whether 'because I want it to be' is a strong addition (it is a reason in form only; the evidence board shows what facts look like), and what helps when talk has drifted (asking more about the cup versus a linking question). A.reveal shows the learner's prediction against the result.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions across new topics (homework, park bins, trees, school trip, museum bus, pets) with options rotated each round. Each wrong option carries a tag with its own message: repeat, offtopic, vague, noreason, drift, rude and person, so the feedback names the exact discussion slip rather than just 'wrong'. A streak counter rewards consistency.

readability.evidence: Learner text uses short sentences and concrete school examples (lunch break, reading corner, benches). validate_lessons reports readability within the learner limits for kid and adult text. Technical terms (exploratory talk, SL.5.1c) stay in the adult section; learners see plain phrases like 'build on', 'follow-up question' and 'steer it back'.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph adds one move: the goal of a discussion, building versus repeating with a worked pair of replies, follow-up questions plus specific questions and evidence, and steering drift back. Adult paragraphs give the standard, sentence starters, a named list of mistakes and the lab summary with a home game. gate_content passes with no filler phrases and low overlap.

mobile.evidence: Checked at 360 px Android and iPhone 13 in both themes and on desktop: all cards are full-width rows at least 44 px tall, text wraps inside cards, bubbles never overlap, and the drift pill sits below the meter. Every canvas action also has a button below the canvas, drag is optional (tap works for replies, facts and bins), and the phone canvas is taller (tall 1.45) so the five question rows fit.

accessibility.evidence: axe scans at every step before and after Show me in light and dark themes on desktop and iPhone report zero violations. Every button has an aria-label with the full reply, question or fact text, the canvas aria-label mirrors each spoken update, feedback uses a polite live region, and success and error states use both colour and text (tick marks, 'too vague' and 'not about Leo's idea' pills).

sources: Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts, Speaking and Listening SL.5.1c (pose and respond to specific questions by making comments that contribute to the discussion and elaborate on the remarks of others)
